nodes.name: actions.ts
nodes.summary: Server actions for the Athena assistant: conversation CRUD and pinning, confirming or rejecting pending write actions, memory and knowledge entries, settings, model/effort updates, and log clearing.

nodes.name: listConversations
nodes.summary: Returns the session list for the current user.

nodes.name: loadConversation
nodes.summary: Server action: requires a logged-in user and loads the messages plus action statuses/results of one conversation via ladeSessionZustand; returns an empty state when unauthenticated.

nodes.name: renameConversation
nodes.summary: Server action: trims and caps the title at 120 chars, rejects empty, updates ai_conversations scoped to the user, writes a session.rename AI log and revalidates /assistant.

nodes.name: deleteConversation
nodes.summary: Server action: logs session.delete first (ai_logs would lose its conversation link afterwards), then deletes the user's ai_conversations row and revalidates /assistant.

nodes.name: togglePinConversation
nodes.summary: Server action: sets the pinned flag on the user's ai_conversations row and revalidates /assistant; returns an error for unauthenticated users or DB failures.

nodes.name: confirmPendingAction
nodes.summary: Executes a pending write action proposed by the assistant after user confirmation and records the outcome.

nodes.name: signValuableImage
nodes.summary: Creates a signed URL for a generated image.

nodes.name: rejectPendingAction
nodes.summary: Server action: flips a still-pending ai_pending_actions row of the user to rejected with resolved_at, errors if already decided, logs action.rejected and revalidates /assistant.

nodes.name: upsertMemory
nodes.summary: Server action: validates slug key and non-empty content from FormData, upserts ai_memories on user_id,key with source user (outweighs agent-written entries), logs memory.write and revalidates /assistant/memory.

nodes.name: deleteMemory
nodes.summary: Server action: deletes the user's ai_memories row by id, logs memory.delete with the removed key and revalidates /assistant/memory.

nodes.name: saveKnowledgeEntry
nodes.summary: Server action: validates title and content, parses up to 10 comma-separated tags and optional source URL, then updates (if id given) or inserts (source user) an ai_knowledge row; logs and revalidates.

nodes.name: deleteKnowledgeEntry
nodes.summary: Server action: deletes the user's ai_knowledge row by id, logs knowledge.delete with its title and revalidates /assistant/knowledge.

nodes.name: toggleKnowledgePin
nodes.summary: Server action: sets the pinned flag on the user's ai_knowledge row and revalidates /assistant/knowledge.

nodes.name: saveAthenaSettings
nodes.summary: Server action: validates step limit (1-60), daily cap, persona against ATHENA_PERSONAS and text lengths, stores NULL when persona text equals the template, then upserts ai_settings for the user.

nodes.name: updateAthenaModelEffort
nodes.summary: Server action: merges a partial model/effort patch with current ai_settings (getAthenaSettings) and upserts the full row on user_id, then revalidates /assistant/settings.

nodes.name: clearLogs
nodes.summary: Server action: deletes the user's ai_logs older than the given number of days (cutoff computed from now) and revalidates /assistant/logs.

nodes.name: proxy
nodes.summary: Skips public routes, then builds a Supabase server client over request cookies, refreshes the session via getUser, and redirects to /login after signOut when the refresh token is missing or the status is 400.

nodes.name: stripKrakenSuffix

nodes.name: toGeckoId
nodes.summary: Maps an asset symbol to a CoinGecko id using the ticker table, falling back to the lowercased bare symbol.

nodes.name: isDueToday
nodes.summary: Decides whether a recurring contract is due today from start date, weekly/biweekly day interval or monthly/quarterly/biannual/yearly month interval, honoring an optional billing day.

nodes.name: findTicker

nodes.name: fetchQuote

nodes.name: getSettings

tour.title: Project Overview and Root Layout
tour.description: Athena Finance is a private finance and investing web app built on Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, Tailwind and Supabase. The tour starts at the root layout, which defines fonts, metadata and the HTML shell that wraps every route, and at the README and CLAUDE.md, which document the stack and working rules. Package and Vercel config show how the app is built and deployed.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js App Router layouts nest: the root layout renders once and every route segment, including route groups like (dashboard), is rendered inside its children slot.

tour.title: Session Proxy and Supabase Clients
tour.description: Authentication rests on Supabase SSR. The proxy (Next.js middleware) refreshes the session cookie on every non-public request, while separate browser and server client factories give components and server code correctly typed access to the database. The server client, the most depended-on file in the repo, also exposes a request-cached user lookup that layouts and actions reuse.
tour.languageLesson: Wrapping a lookup in React cache() deduplicates it within a single server request, so many components can call getAuthUser without repeated network round trips.

tour.title: Login and the Protected Dashboard Shell
tour.description: Building on the Supabase clients, the login page is a server component that reads error and message search params, and its server actions handle sign-in, sign-up and sign-out with validated input. The (dashboard) layout redirects unauthenticated visitors to /login and wraps all protected pages in the client-side AppShell, which provides the sidebar, mobile drawer and page transitions.

tour.title: API Guards and Zod Validation
tour.description: Every route handler and server action funnels untrusted input through a small shared toolkit. parse.ts is a framework-free zod core with German error messages, schemas.ts offers reusable building blocks (uuid, ISO date, bounded money), and validate.ts adapts them to 400 responses. auth.ts supplies the requireUser and requireCron guards, and cron checks fail closed when the secret is missing.
tour.languageLesson: Keeping pure logic (parse.ts, cron-auth.ts) free of framework imports lets it be unit-tested with the plain node:test runner, as the sibling .test.ts files do.

tour.title: Data Access Layer
tour.description: Instead of scattering queries across pages, src/lib/data holds pure functions that take a Supabase client and user id and return typed rows. Modules such as overview, finance-accounts, finance-transactions and finance-planning cover the main domains, and the generated database types keep results type-safe. Row Level Security in the database remains the real security boundary behind these helpers.

tour.title: Dashboard Page and Server Actions
tour.description: The dashboard page is a server component that uses the data layer to fetch accounts, transactions, debts, goals and crypto before rendering. Mutations live in colocated server actions such as accounts, contracts and transactions actions, each validating FormData with the zod helpers from the previous steps before writing to Supabase. This split, server components for reads and actions for writes, is the pattern across the whole finance area.
tour.languageLesson: Server Actions are async functions marked with a use server directive that can be passed to forms; they run on the server but are invoked from the client, so they must re-validate input and re-check the user.

tour.title: Finance Core Pages and Forms
tour.description: Building on the data access layer from Step 5 and the dashboard shell from Step 6, the finance area in the Pages & Routing and UI Components layers covers accounts, transactions, categories, budget, contracts, debts and goals. Each route is a Server Component page that reads through src/lib/data/finance-*.ts, while forms such as account-form.tsx and transaction-form.tsx are Client Components that post to colocated actions.ts Server Actions. Pure helpers like wiederkehrend.ts and category-groups.ts keep business rules testable outside React.

tour.title: Analysis and Cash-Flow Views
tour.description: The analysis area turns the same transactions into period-based insight: the overview page, the verlauf (history) view and the banking view. Shared selectors (AnalysePeriodSelector, AnalyseAccountSelector) drive the period, and src/lib/analyseData.ts aggregates the rows that feed charts like GeldflussChart, KategorienChart, MonatsVergleich and the CashflowKalender. Heavy chart implementations are split into -impl files so they can be lazy-loaded on the client.

tour.title: Depot and Funds
tour.description: The depot module tracks fund holdings, savings plans and prices. The depot page and DepotDashboard render data loaded through src/lib/data/depot.ts, while src/app/actions/depot.ts handles mutations and the depot API routes serve holdings and live prices. savingsPlanChecker.ts and the depot tables (depots, depot_holdings, savings_plans, fund_prices) tie it to the scheduled jobs covered later.

tour.title: Inventory of Valuables
tour.description: The inventar area catalogs physical valuables such as watches or art, with photos and value history. The page and InventoryClient render data from src/lib/data/inventar.ts, forms and actions create and edit items, and src/lib/valuables.ts holds the shared types and category rules. AI artwork generation lives in src/lib/inventar/artwork.ts behind the /api/inventar/artwork route, backed by the valuables tables.

tour.title: Strategy, Indicators and Combos
tour.description: The strategy area lets you define trading indicators, combine them into combos and strategies, and record test performance. Routes under strategy/ share a layout and read through src/lib/data/strategy.ts, with Server Actions per sub-area and forms and tables in src/components/strategy. It implements the Masterclass investing framework as data, and the checklist panel supports rule-based decisions.

tour.title: Crypto and Kraken
tour.description: The crypto area combines a coin registry and a CoinGecko price client with pure portfolio logic: calculateRebalancing computes target deviations and buildRebalancePlan turns them into executable order legs. The Kraken modules sign requests, sync balances and trades, compute average cost basis, and are the only code that places orders, with a six-hourly cron route driving the sync.

tour.title: Bank Sync with the FinTS Sidecar
tour.description: German bank data is fetched by a Python sidecar built on python-fints. The Node service spawns it as a process, passes persisted client state and maps its output to typed accounts, transactions and holdings, while SCA helpers detect when strong customer authentication is required. Cron and user-triggered API routes share this flow.
tour.languageLesson: A sidecar process isolates a library from another ecosystem: Node exchanges JSON over stdout and exit codes with the Python script instead of reimplementing the FinTS protocol.

tour.title: Tax Engine and Reports
tour.description: The tax module is a set of pure, well-tested functions: tarif.ts implements the section 32a EStG income tax tariff, euer.ts distributes bookings onto Anlage EUER lines, and position.ts derives profit and tax position. The reports module builds deterministic report data, renders HTML and PDF, stores the file and emails it through a monthly cron route.

tour.title: Athena AI Assistant
tour.description: Athena is a streaming chat assistant behind a single POST route that authenticates, enforces a daily cap and builds a per-request toolbelt. Read-only tools query the user's data, while every write is a proposal generated from the action registry, so nothing changes until the user confirms in the UI. The system prompt combines a cacheable core, persona, app atlas and user memory.
tour.languageLesson: The confirmation flow is a human-in-the-loop pattern: the model may only emit a typed proposal, and a separate server action executes it after explicit approval.

tour.title: Landing Page
tour.description: The public landing page is composed from server sections plus small client islands. Server components render the static editorial content, while islands such as Reveal handle scroll animation, keeping client JavaScript limited to interactivity. Shared design tokens drive colors and typography, and a waitlist server action stores signups.
tour.languageLesson: Islands architecture: a server component can import a small use-client component, so only that leaf ships JavaScript to the browser.

tour.title: Scheduled Jobs and Cron
tour.description: Recurring work runs on two schedulers. Vercel cron, configured in vercel.json, calls route handlers under src/app/api/cron/ (bank-sync, kraken-sync, monthly-report and the retired book-contracts, daily-snapshot, execute-savings-plans stubs that return 410), each guarded by cron-auth.ts, while the Python function api/bank-sync.py serves the FinTS sync. Supabase pg_cron invokes the Edge Functions daily-snapshot, execute-contracts, execute-savings-plans and fetch-fund-price, which took over those duties from Vercel.

tour.title: Database, Views and Edge Functions
tour.description: The Supabase migrations define the schema with RLS: the unified_transactions view merges bank and manual bookings, and the later balance and valuation views compute account balance sums, hardened with security_invoker. Scheduled Edge Functions run contracts and the daily snapshot inside Supabase, replacing the decommissioned Vercel cron routes.
tour.languageLesson: SQL views declared with security_invoker run with the caller's privileges, so RLS on the underlying tables still applies.
